description: Two resonant lowpass filters fed the same signal, with the second subtracted from the first to give a two-peaked bandpass; built to be pinged with stepped voltages at high resonance

params.text: Sets the cutoff of filter A, 20Hz to 20kHz, and comes up at the bottom of that range
Sets the cutoff of filter B, 20Hz to 20kHz, and comes up at the top of that range
Sets the resonance of both filters at once, 0 to 1; the band marked on the panel is the part of the travel that pings well
Attenuates and inverts the RES jack, -1 to 1, before that voltage reaches the resonance of both filters
Sends some of the input signal to filter A's own cutoff, -1 to 1
Sends some of the input signal to filter B's own cutoff, -1 to 1
Scales everything modulating filter A's cutoff together, -1 to 1, so it can attenuate or invert the whole sum
Scales everything modulating filter B's cutoff together, -1 to 1, so it can attenuate or invert the whole sum
Attenuates and inverts the FM A jack, -1 to 1, before the FM A knob scales it
Attenuates and inverts the FM B jack, -1 to 1, before the FM B knob scales it
Sends some of filter B's output to filter A's cutoff, -1 to 1
Chooses how steep both filters are: two poles for 12dB per octave, three for 18dB, four for 24dB
Crossfades the output from filter A's lowpass alone at 0 to the full two-peaked response at 1
Attenuates and inverts the LP-TWP jack, -1 to 1, before that voltage is added to the LP-TWP knob

inputs.text: Moves the resonance of both filters, scaled by its attenuverter and added to the RES knob
One volt per octave on filter A's cutoff, added with no attenuverter in the way
One volt per octave on filter B's cutoff, added with no attenuverter in the way
Modulates filter A's cutoff, scaled by its own attenuverter and then by the FM A knob; it also feeds filter B while the FM B jack has no cable
Modulates filter B's cutoff, scaled by its own attenuverter and then by the FM B knob
The signal both filters are fed; its channel count sets the polyphony of the whole module
Divided by 10, scaled by its attenuverter and added to the LP-TWP knob, the total clamped to 0 and 1

outputs.text: Filter A's output minus filter B's, the subtraction scaled by the LP-TWP setting, clamped to -12V and 12V

notes: every route to a cutoff is summed and then capped, so neither filter can be pushed above the 20kHz its knob already reaches at the top
a tiny amount of noise is added to the input inside each filter, which is what lets a high resonance setting break into self-oscillation with nothing patched
the filter core is the one from Audible Instruments' Liquid Filter, with a three-pole output added for the 18dB setting
